text:
Ravi S.: follow-up from today's allocation ergonomics sync — observed odd tail regens when we combine coalesce buffering + aggressive demote. thinking we should discuss policy ordering + CPU affinity for background coalesce work.

Elena: can you paste the trace? curious if it's NVMe or CPU contention.

Ravi S.: snippet in perf bucket: `s3://redwood-perf/alloc-ergo/2026-04-02/coalesce-demote-trace.tar.gz`. TL;DR: background coalesce worker stealing CPU from infer workers during short spikes -> scheduler latency -> request slowdowns.

Tom S.: yep that pattern rings a bell. we spawn coalescers on same cgroups as background reclaimers; when many small pages pile up the ring buffer flushes and the kernel schedules the flush thread on inference core.

Marta R.: two obvious levers: pin coalescer threads to low-priority CPUs (affinity + SCHED_IDLE) or perform coalesce in the IO threadpool off the hot path with cooperative yielding.

Elena: caution: SCHED_IDLE can delay coalesce long enough to cause NVMe queue pileups if IO capacity is limited. we need a smarter policy: dynamic cpu assignment based on current nvme queue depth + tail SLO signals.

Ravi S.: propose hybrid policy:
```
if nvme_qd < Q_low and tail_slo_ok:
  run_coalesce_lowprio()
elif nvme_qd < Q_high:
  run_coalesce_shared_cpu()
else:
  throttle_coalesce()+defer
```
Where Q_low/Q_high are tunables per-pool.

Tom S.: sounds good. add: when deferring, mark demote candidate pages with `deferred_coalesce=true` so the next allocation that touches that region can do an opportunistic inline coalesce (piggyback). minimizes background work.

Elena: piggybacking is great but ensure we don't create write amplification on the fast path. inline piggyback should only merge metadata and mark for batched write; actual write can still be queued to IO pool.

Marta R.: agreed. also consider low-memory handoff: if pool memory pressure crosses `mem_crit_pct`, we should bypass coalescer and force synchronous flushes to free memory. safety wins over latency.

Ravi S.: adding config sketch:
```
coalesce_policy:
  q_low: 8
  q_high: 32
  inline_piggyback_threshold: 4
  mem_crit_pct: 92
  cpu_affinity_mode: dynamic|pinned|idle
```
Defaults: dynamic.

Tom S.: from implementation POV: add fast-path hint bits on page descriptors, and a small fixed-size per-NUMA ring for coalesce batching to avoid allocations. already discussed that for coalescer so reuse.

Elena: metrics: coalesce_cpu_ms, coalesce_defer_count, inline_piggyback_hits, nvme_qd_by_pool, forced_sync_flushes. critical for canary rollback decisions.

qa-bot: perf-test queued: alloc-coalesce-affinity-2026-04-05  run config attached.

Marta R.: canary criteria: if request p99 increases >10% during coalesce bursts OR mem pressure leads to >3 forced sync flushes/sec, abort. also track tenant fairness: if one tenant sees >2x p99 vs baseline, flag.

Ravi S.: I'll open RFC follow-up PR with the policy + code pointers. Tom, can you stub the hint-bit changes? Elena, can you wire the nvme_qd signal into the scheduler gate?

Tom S.: will do, stub PR incoming.

Elena: wiring nvme_qd is straightforward via existing iostats sampler; will add per-pool smoothing (EWMA).

Marta R.: thanks. add a short note in docs about "deferred_coalesce" semantics so SRE and customers understand behavior for Dedicated pools.

Ravi S.: will include that. ok closing thread — follow-ups in PR and perf job results. :thumbsup:
